text:
This looks like February 2021. The unemployment rate is 6.3%, which matches January 2021. The fed funds rate is 0.07% and the 10-year yield is 1.54%, which fits late February 2021, when the 10-year was about 1.4%. A VIX near 28.9 also fits late February 2021, and gold fell 6.2% that month.

Other figures fit as well. Headline CPI of 1.37% matches January 2021 (1.4%), and core CPI of 1.4% matches too. US equities returned +30% over 12 months and the 10-year yield rose 0.70 points over 3 months. The payroll average over 3 months is +28.67k, which is consistent with the weak job gains of late 2020 and January 2021.

Industrial production is -1.83% year on year, which fits January 2021 (roughly -1.8%). Gold's one-month drop of 6.2% matches February 2021, as does the 20-year-plus Treasury loss of 6.8%.

The snapshot therefore describes February 2021.
